bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day drives street-wide PT lifts; FY28 rev target $20B, FY31 $70-90B
bullets.body: Marvell raised its FY28 revenue target to $20B (vs. prior ~$18B and consensus $18.2B) and set a FY31 long-term model of $70-90B revenue at 55-60% CAGR, >$30 EPS, and >36% FCF margin. Custom XPU revenue targeted at $12B+ in FY29 and ~$30B midpoint by FY31. Sell-side consensus is 90% Buy; average PT lifted +13% to $337 (Piper to $400, Stifel to $370); JPM separately reiterates OW with credible path to $35+ EPS by CY30.

bullets.title: MU: Taiwan union authorizes strike; DA Davidson raises PT to $3,000 on AI memory upcycle
bullets.body: Micron's Taiwan labor union voted to authorize a strike over an FY26 bonus dispute, creating a near-term supply-risk overhang (stock -2.6% pre-market). Separately, DA Davidson raised its PT from $2,100 to $3,000, arguing AI workloads are increasingly memory-constrained and strategic contracts (~50% of volume) provide demand visibility through 2027-28; a larger buyback and potential dividend increase flagged for the December board meeting.

bullets.title: SPOT: Audiobooks global rollout = meaningful 2027 gross margin tailwind; Citi Buy, $620 PT
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy with a $620 PT (27% upside, ~27x 2027E FCF). Spotify is expanding audiobooks to ~10 new markets covering 20-25% of Premium subs by end of FY26; historical pattern implies ~10% price hike ~2 quarters post-launch (mid-2027), adding ~€0.10 to ARPU with ~90% gross profit flowthrough. Modest 4Q26 margin headwind expected, followed by expansion through 2027.

bullets.title: HUT: UBS Buy, $143 PT; River Bend Phase 1 on time/budget, multi-GW expansion path clear
bullets.body: UBS reiterates Buy on Hut 8 after a River Bend site visit: Phase 1 (330MW gross / 245MW IT) has ~1,100 workers on site with structural steel largely complete; first 65MW IT data hall expected online 2Q27. Phase 2 land clearing has begun with behind-the-meter generation as the likely power bridge. Recent rate increases have not impacted AI data center demand; PT $143 on 22x 2028E EBITDA.

bullets.title: RBLX: -3.6% pre-market on Unity-Google 'Playground' AI gaming platform; UBS Neutral
bullets.body: Unity is partnering with Google to launch an AI gaming platform ('Playground') targeting 18+ users with high-fidelity 3D graphics in 2026, a direct competitive threat. UBS maintains Neutral on Roblox, noting the company retains a first-mover advantage with its integrated end-to-end development-through-monetization offering, but says the stock will remain sensitive to competitive headline risk.

bullets.title: CEG/VST/TLN: Sentiment pivot on data center PPA execution; GOOGL signs new CEG power deal
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes IPPs CEG, VST, and TLN are trading with what appears to be no incremental contracting upside priced in, despite a positive sentiment pivot around ability to execute data center PPAs without 1-for-1 PJM capacity requirements. GOOGL separately signed a new power deal with CEG. CEG -3.6% in pre-market alongside broader data-center power complex weakness.

bullets.title: CRWV: JPM hosts joint equity/credit call; AI capex sustainability debate intensifies
bullets.body: JPMorgan convened a joint equity and credit discussion on CoreWeave today (analysts Chatterjee + Egan) addressing business fundamentals and capital structure. Separately, 22V flagged that $400-600B of frontier-lab ARR by end-2027 is the minimum needed to underwrite capex through 2028-29, and called Anthropic's IPO revenue commentary the single most important near-term catalyst for AI buildout names.

bullets.title: CHTR/CMCSA: TD Cowen keeps Buys despite cable headwinds; KeyBanc more negative, UW CMCSA
bullets.body: TD Cowen previews Q3 cable with a cautious near-term outlook—FTTH and FWA adding pressure, CMCSA guiding to above-expected subscriber losses—but maintains Buy on both CHTR and CMCSA citing attractive valuations. KeyBanc is more bearish: its Q3 broadband survey finds fiber and FWA offer faster speeds at lower prices, keeps CHTR at Sector Weight and CMCSA at Underweight, while upgrading T and TMUS to Overweight.

bullets.title: VZ/T: TD Cowen sees positive Q3 wireless fundamentals; rates, Starlink, AI Muse are overhangs
bullets.body: TD Cowen previews Q3 wireless as largely positive—tame competition, muted churn, carriers reiterating guidance—but flags three investor concerns: rising interest rates, Starlink Mobile launch uncertainty, and Meta's AI Muse price-search tool. Ratings: TMUS Buy, VZ Buy, T Hold. Competitive threats seen as manageable but requiring multiple quarters to defuse.

bullets.title: NVDA: Index concentration masking broader weakness; SpaceX GPU build-out creates new supply competition
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes Nvidia's outsized index weight keeps S&P 500 at all-time highs (risk range 7,676-7,851) while the broader market deteriorates. More structurally, SpaceX built 200k GPU / ~300-500MW of compute capacity in 9 months vs. the industry's typical 18-36 months for 100MW, creating a faster and potentially cheaper competing supply source that is pressuring neocloud and DC operator stocks.

bullets.title: AFRM: JPM sees F1Q27 as trough volume quarter; mix shift to interest-bearing accretive to margins
bullets.body: JPM flags AFRM's fiscal Q1 2027 as the slowest volume growth quarter, implying upside in the second half. The mix shift toward interest-bearing originations is described as margin accretive. JPM favors MA, V, AFRM, and TOST into payments earnings season while viewing PYPL, FIS, GPN, and FISV as requiring management or portfolio action to work.

bullets.title: ORCL/CRM: KeyBanc sees agentic AI as opportunity for incumbents with contextual data moats
bullets.body: KeyBanc's ScaleUp AI event takeaway: only 40% of CIOs can quantify clear AI value, creating a vendor opportunity. Centralized unified data layers are the critical foundation for agentic AI; Oracle and Databricks are cited as well-positioned. The software moat is shifting from product ownership to speed of continuous AI-driven innovation, posing risk to incumbents that fail to modernize workflows.

bullets.title: NFLX: JPM OW maintained; focus on content slate, engagement, and 2027 margin expansion
bullets.body: JPMorgan reiterates Overweight on Netflix heading into 3Q earnings season, with focus areas on the content slate, engagement trends, and the path to margin expansion in 2027. Netflix is also listed among Piper Sandler's Overweight names in internet/digital media coverage.

bullets.title: TTWO: UBS Buy; Xbox reportedly secured non-exclusive GTA VI streaming rights
bullets.body: Press reports suggest Xbox secured non-exclusive GTA VI streaming rights (no PC), which Take-Two has not confirmed. UBS maintains Buy, noting streaming could broaden accessibility at a time of rising console prices and follows a recently renewed Xbox agreement with TTWO.

bullets.title: GOOGL/META: $1.8B Virtual Biology Initiative; META developing Personal Agent Protocol with Sierra
bullets.body: Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs, and Meta are collectively investing $300M in a Virtual Biology Initiative as part of a broader $1.8B international collaboration for AI-driven disease prediction. Separately, Sierra announced the Personal Agent Protocol open standard for personal AI agents, developed in partnership with Meta.

bullets.title: APP/U: Jefferies hosting webinar 10/8 on mobile gaming ad thesis and earnings positioning
bullets.body: Jefferies is hosting a webinar tomorrow at 10:30am ET specifically on AppLovin and Unity, covering the latest data and positioning into earnings season for both names and the broader mobile gaming advertising space.

bullets.title: CVNA: Financing penetration hits 85% vs. KMX 67%; future growth must come from unit volume
bullets.body: CVNA's financing penetration reached 85% vs. CarMax's 67%, making the model increasingly dependent on third-party loan buyers. Analysts note future growth must now come from unit volume rather than further financing attach-rate expansion.

bullets.title: TXN: Cantor Fitzgerald analog preview; AI demand and tight CY27 supply support pricing
bullets.body: Cantor Fitzgerald previews analog chips positively: AI-related demand is driving positive cyclicality with tight market conditions expected through CY27 supporting pricing upside. Analyst preference order is ADI > NXPI > MCHP > TXN > ON; TXN rated Neutral with a $340 PT, while ADI, NXPI, and MCHP are Overweight.

bullets.title: GEV: OPCO names GEV a top power-tech pick into 3Q results
bullets.body: Oppenheimer highlights GEV alongside AMSC, SHLS, and ORA as power technology top picks heading into 3Q earnings. No specific price target or estimate changes were disclosed in the note.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM hosting Platinum Partner expert call 10/19 on agentic commerce, SMB trends, Merchant Solutions
bullets.body: JPMorgan is hosting a webinar on October 19 with Shopify Platinum Partner Zettler Digital (400+ e-commerce brand clients) to discuss Shopify's AI-commerce strategy (Sidekick & Muse), SMB demand cohorts, enterprise adoption cycles, and Merchant Solutions including Shop Pay.
